comparison: Both evaluations strongly support the RNA-seq and RT-qPCR findings (C48-C53, C58-C63). OpenEval emphasizes the converging evidence from multiple experimental approaches including growth assays and Q203 comparison. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the transcriptional response data as 'thorough and well-thought-out' with no concerns raised.

Both evaluations support the genetic complementation and chemical rescue experiments (C71-C79). OpenEval provides comprehensive coverage including epistasis experiments (C80-C86) not explicitly mentioned in peer R2. Peer reviewers highlight the synthetic chalkophore analogue as a particular strength. Complete agreement on the complementation data quality.

Both evaluations support the epistasis analysis (C80-C86) demonstrating bcc:aa3 as the specific target. OpenEval R2 covers broader claims including the main findings (C5-C10, C43). Peer R3 notes the data are 'convincing' for in vitro conditions but identifies a limitation that this is 'not verified under infection conditions.'

Both evaluations support the central conclusion that chalkophore-acquired copper is specifically incorporated into bcc:aa3 oxidase (C5-C10, C43). OpenEval R2 provides detailed experimental support through epistasis and complementation. Peer R9 represents the reviewers' explicit affirmation of this as the main finding, with all reviewers endorsing the conclusion.

Both evaluations support the respiration assay data (C87-C94, C99-C105) showing copper deprivation specifically affects bcc:aa3 oxidase. OpenEval R3 also includes ATP measurements (C106-C108). Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the oxygen consumption data as 'convincing' with no concerns raised about methodology.

Both evaluations support the ATP measurement data (C106-C108) as evidence for oxidative phosphorylation effects. OpenEval R3 provides broader context including respiration assays. Peer R5 explicitly mentions ATP levels alongside oxygen consumption as a strength of the metabolic activity measurements.

Both evaluations support the finding that CtaD protein levels remain stable under copper chelation (C111-C112), contrasting with eukaryotic systems. OpenEval notes the mechanism remains incompletely defined. Peer reviewers do not explicitly discuss this detail but raise no concerns, suggesting implicit acceptance of this supporting data.

Both evaluations strongly support the mouse infection data (C11-C12, C121-C124) showing severe attenuation of the double mutant and rescue by complementation. OpenEval emphasizes adequate sample sizes and statistical significance. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm these findings as 'convincing' with all reviewers endorsing the virulence conclusions.

Both evaluations support the neutrophil depletion and SCID mouse experiments (C13-C14, C125-C128) demonstrating innate immune dependence. OpenEval notes the specific mechanism remains undefined. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm these findings and note the interesting temporal aspect that chalkophore is not required after adaptive immunity onset.

Both evaluations support the main conclusions about chalkophore-mediated respiratory chain protection being critical for virulence (C15-C16, C47, C129, C131-C132). OpenEval emphasizes the multilayered protection model. Peer R9 represents unanimous reviewer affirmation of this central conclusion with explicit endorsements from all reviewers and the editor.

Both evaluations support the multilayered respiratory flexibility model (C16, C47, C148, C157). OpenEval R7 focuses on the main conclusions while peer R10 emphasizes the redundant oxidase system and temporal aspects of infection. Complete agreement on the multilayered protection concept as a key finding.

Both evaluations rate these mechanistic claims as UNCERTAIN (C139, C147). OpenEval notes the epistasis data support bcc:aa3 as sole target in culture but acknowledges limitations about in vivo mechanisms. Peer R11 explicitly identifies as a limitation that the sole target conclusion is 'not verified under infection conditions.' Agreement on uncertainty regarding extrapolation to infection.

Both evaluations support the therapeutic implications (C154, C156) with caveats. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the translation to drug development is speculative and requires substantial additional work. Peer reviewers explicitly endorse these as valid forward-looking implications, though they acknowledge these are not direct experimental findings but rather conclusions from the data.

OpenEval R8 evaluates background claims about the M. tuberculosis respiratory chain (C67-C70, C140-C144) as SUPPORTED, noting this is well-established knowledge from prior studies. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically do not explicitly evaluate background/contextual claims.

OpenEval R9 evaluates claims about Q203, CytBD inhibition, and CytBD's essential role revealed in the double mutant (C64-C66, C150-C153) as SUPPORTED. While peer reviewers discuss CytBD findings in R10, there is no direct peer evaluation of these specific background and CytBD induction claims as a distinct result.

OpenEval R11 evaluates claims about copper affinity, siderophore analogy, and unknown location/timing of copper deprivation in vivo (C133-C138) as UNCERTAIN. These are acknowledged as speculations for future work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers do not separately evaluate these speculative mechanistic details.
